our_title: Fork-mode (de)compression leaks the father's copy of the data buffer
ran: ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 ./tcfc_new_pristine bump_b1.grf p3.gz (pristine fork-mode build): 'ERROR: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks / Direct leak of 131080 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from ... _SCOTCHfileCompress common_file_compress.c:224'; same for decompression. Patched: check_common_file_compress passes in fork mode with leak detection on.
evidence: compress.c:224 '((compptr->bufftab = memAlloc (FILECOMPRESSDATASIZE)) == NULL)' allocated by the father; :190-191 'close (compptr->infdnum); memFree (compptr->bufftab);' run only by the child in fork mode; fileCompressExit (:122) frees compptr only.

fix_options.label: A. Father frees the buffer right after fork()
fix_options.summary: memFree (compptr->bufftab) in the 'default:' branch of both fork switches.
fix_options.tested: fork-mode check_common_file_compress with detect_leaks=1 passes; gpart with two .gz outputs reports no leak.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: two-line fix in the fork branch he already owns

fix_options.label: B. Allocate the buffer in the task (thread/child) instead of the father
fix_options.tradeoffs: Allocation failure could then no longer be reported to the caller of fileBlockOpen().

our_title: bgraphBipartGaLoop() uses sizeof (UINT) bits of each random value (bytes mistaken for bits)
why_not_run: behavioural only: a fix changes GA results, which is the maintainer's call; GA ('a' bipartitioning method) is not in any default strategy
evidence: 'randnbr = MIN (sizeof (UINT), partnum);       /* Compute useable slices   */' with 'demetab[-- partnum] = (GraphPart) (randval & 1); randval >>= 1;' consuming one bit per slice: 4 or 8 bits of each 64-bit draw are used.

fix_options.label: A. Use UINT64 and sizeof (UINT64) << 3 slices
fix_options.tested: untested: changes GA outputs by design
fix_options.tradeoffs: 8x fewer generator calls when filling demes; GA results change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: his decision (determinism of GA across versions)

fix_options.label: B. Leave as is
fix_options.summary: Document that only the low bits are used.

our_title: gz (de)compression closes the descriptor with gzclose() but leaves the FILE* open
read_only: common_file_compress.c:326-341, common_file_decompress.c:322-335 vs the bz2/lzma twins (:306, :416 fclose (compptr->oustptr))
why_not_run: no observable effect in the tools (process exits right after); glibc's exit does not close descriptors of stale streams
evidence: compress.c:326 'gzdopen (fileno (compptr->oustptr), "wb")' and :341 'gzclose (encoptr);                              /* Closes oustptr */' — gzclose closes the descriptor only; the FILE* oustptr stays in stdio's list with a dead (reusable) descriptor number, unlike the bz2/lzma paths which fclose() it.

fix_options.label: A. gzdopen (dup (fileno (oustptr))) then fclose (oustptr) as the other two formats do
fix_options.summary: Keeps stdio and zlib ownership separate.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: mirrors his 'Do as zlib does' comment in the twins, the other way round

fix_options.label: B. Leave as is
fix_options.tradeoffs: stale FILE* per compressed stream in long-running programs
